Reference Guide

Finding your way around the Sales Dashboard

This report has six pages — Dashboard, Sales Trend, Product Images, L12M Customer Buys, Collection Sales, and Cancelled Container Orders — that all work together and share your filters (with one exception — see below). This guide walks through what each page shows you and how to get the most out of it.

01 — Start here

Getting started

Signing in takes two fields, and the report remembers you until you sign out.

Signing in

Choose your name from the dropdown, enter your password, and select Sign In. Click Show next to the password field if you want to check what you typed before submitting.

Tip Your browser may offer to save this password for next time — that's safe to accept. You'll stay signed in as you move between pages until you either sign out or close every window of your browser.

Getting around

Once you're in, the navy bar at the top is always there. It has seven things on it:

Dashboard
Where you land after signing in. A high-level summary of your book of business, plus your rank on the company leaderboard.
Sales Trend
Month-by-month detail for every group you sell, with a full export.
Product Images
A searchable photo library, filterable to what one or more customers have bought.
L12M Customer Buys
Which product groups any customer — not just your own — has bought in the last 12 months, and how two customers' buying compares.
Collection Sales
What you're missing — SKUs in your best-selling groups you haven't sold yet, and cross-sell opportunities in other categories.
Cancelled Container Orders
Your cancelled container orders this year — by customer, category, group, and warehouse, with credit hold and override flags.
Daily Sales Report
Only shown if one's set up for you — downloads your daily Excel snapshot directly.
02 — The six pages

The Dashboard page

Your landing page. KPIs, your leaderboard rank, trend charts, an auto-written summary, and a look at how your top groups stack up against the whole company.

KPI cards

Across the top: this year's and last year's Invoiced and Written totals, the year-over-year change, Total Open Orders, and how many of your customers are trending up versus down. Everything here is year-to-date through today's date, compared to the same point last year.

Your Sales Rank

The navy card below the KPIs shows where you rank company-wide on YTD Invoiced sales. Select it — or View Leaderboard — to open the full leaderboard, with a second tab for Most Improved (YOY): who's grown the fastest since last year. Your own row is highlighted wherever you appear.

The two charts

Invoiced Sales by Month and Written Sales by Month compare this year's bars against last year's for every month. Hover over any bar for the exact dollar amount — on this year's bars, the tooltip also shows the year-over-year percentage change for that month.

Performance Analysis

A short written summary, regenerated automatically from your current numbers. It calls out your biggest customer movers, new and lost customers, and which categories are growing or shrinking — a quick way to catch something worth a phone call before you dig into the tables.

Filtering to one or more customers

Use the Customer dropdown above the charts to narrow everything on the page — KPIs, charts, summary, and every table below — down to one account, or several at once. See Picking more than one below for how the checkbox list works.

Filtering by Category, Subcategory, Vendor, and SPIN

Four more dropdowns next to Customer narrow the same KPIs, charts, summary, and tables: Category and Subcategory (e.g. Main Bedroom → Beds), Vendor down to a single manufacturer — useful for questions like "how is Vendor X doing across my whole book" without switching to Sales Trend — and SPIN. None of these four carry over to the other pages — each is local to whichever page you set it on (see Filters that follow you).

Export Dashboard The green button next to the filters downloads everything on this page — KPI cards, the summary, and every table — as a formatted Excel workbook, scoped to whatever Customer/Category/Subcategory/Vendor/SPIN selections you currently have.

Sales by Site, Customer, Category, and Subcategory

Four breakdown tables beneath the charts, each with a Sales Mix column showing what share of your total business that row represents.

Negative figures A negative dollar figure in any of these tables — Invoiced YTD, Invoiced LY YTD, Written YTD, or Written LY YTD — shows in red, the same red used for a declining year-over-year percentage.

Top Groups by Category

To the right, every group you've sold in each of the four categories — Main Bedroom, Living Room, Dining Room, and Others — sorted by Invoiced Sales YTD in a scrollable list. Next to each of your tables sits a narrower Company Top 10 list: the company's own top-performing groups for that same category, shown as Sales Mix only, so you can scan the two side by side.

Filtering by Category narrows both sides down to just the matching bucket — the other three go blank. Filtering to a single Subcategory does the same for your own table, and switches Company Top 10 to that subcategory's own ranking too. Select more than one Subcategory at once, though, and Company Top 10 falls back to its whole-category view — combining several subcategories into one ranking isn't something that list can show.

Reading the highlights

Rows in the Company Top 10 list are shaded to flag where you have room to grow:

Under-indexing — you sell it, but below the company's share Missing — no sales for this group yet this year

A row with no shading means you're already at or above the company's share for that group — nothing to flag. Hover over any shaded row to see the exact percentages behind the highlight.

Export Entire Group List The Top 10 tables cap at 10 rows to stay readable on screen. The green button above them exports the complete group list for all four categories to Excel, one tab per category, if you need to see everything.
02 — The six pages

The Sales Trend page

The month-by-month detail behind your numbers, one row per group, with a full Excel export.

Customer, Category, Subcategory, Vendor, and SPIN filters

Narrow the whole page to one or more customers, categories, subcategories, a manufacturer, or SPIN, in any combination. The KPI cards, summary, and table below all update together. Only Customer follows you to the other pages — Category, Subcategory, Vendor, and SPIN are all local to this page (see Filters that follow you).

The monthly table

Every group you sell gets a row, with last year's months on the left and this year's on the right, followed by YTD totals, year-over-year trend, Total Open, and Next 3 Months Open. Click any column header to sort by it — click again to reverse the sort. The table scrolls horizontally, so scroll right to see everything past the current-year months.

Export to Excel Downloads a formatted workbook matching whatever Customer/Category/Subcategory/Vendor/SPIN filters you currently have set, with a Summary tab (KPI cards + narrative) and the full data table.

Daily Sales Report

If you have one set up, a button appears in the top bar next to Sign Out. It downloads your Daily Sales Excel file directly — the same file you'd otherwise get emailed.

02 — The six pages

The Product Images page

A searchable photo library for every group, filterable down to what one or more customers have actually bought.

Search and filters

Type a group name into the search box, or narrow the grid with the Category dropdown. The Customer dropdown only lists your own customers, and selecting one or more filters the grid down to groups those customers have ordered this year — invoiced or still open, either counts.

Filtering by Vendor

The Vendor dropdown narrows the grid down to photos sourced from a single manufacturer — pulled straight from the same Master SKUs sheet the rest of this page's photos come from, so it always covers every image, not just ones you've personally sold.

Sort By

The Sort dropdown next to the filters switches the grid between alphabetical (A to Z) and Sales $, highest YTD first — handy for quickly finding your best sellers' photos.

Using an image

Click any photo to open the full-size lifestyle image in a new tab — handy to pull up on a call or drop into an email while you're talking through options with a customer.

02 — The six pages

The L12M Customer Buys page

Which product groups any customer — company-wide, not just your own — has bought in the last 12 months.

Browsing one customer

Select any customer from the Customer filter to see every Category they've purchased from, each collapsed into a card you can expand for the full list of Groups. Nothing shows until you pick a customer — there's no "all customers at once" view here, since that would just be the master group list with no customer attached.

Comparing two customers

Add a second customer in Compare To and each category splits into two columns: the first customer's full group list on the left, the second customer's full group list on the right. Every group that both customers buy is highlighted green in both columns; a group only one of them buys is highlighted red on that side — so instead of just a one-way gap list, you get a real side-by-side picture of where their assortments overlap and where they diverge. If the second customer has bought into a whole category the first one hasn't touched at all, that category still shows up with an empty left column and a full (red) list on the right, so a completely open category isn't easy to miss.

Warehouse, Category, and Sales Rep filters

Three more filters narrow both columns at once — useful for questions like "what has this customer bought out of the Vietnam warehouse" or checking one category at a time instead of scrolling the full list.

Export to Excel Downloads the current Customer (and Compare To, if set) selection as one flat table — Category, Customer, Group, and Status (Shared/Unique when comparing) — matching whatever you're looking at on screen.
02 — The six pages

The Collection Sales page

What you're missing — and where else you could be selling groups you're already good at.

How it's built

This page ranks your top 30 (Category, Group) combinations by YTD invoiced sales. Every one of them is something you're already selling well — the page is about finding the gaps and the neighboring opportunities around your strengths, not your weak spots.

Expanding a group

Select any bar to expand it. Underneath, every SKU that exists in that group is split into two columns: Sold on the left (what you've already sold this customer set), Missing on the right (SKUs in that same group you haven't sold at all). A count above each side tells you how many, out of the total.

Same Group in Other Categories

Group names sometimes exist under more than one category — the same style might appear in both Main Bedroom and Living Room, for example. When that's true, this section shows the same Sold/Missing split for that other category, so you can see whether a group you're already good at is worth pitching somewhere you haven't touched it yet.

Customer filter

Use the Customer dropdown to scope the whole page to one or more accounts. This isn't just a display filter — the top 30 ranking and every Sold/Missing split recalculate for exactly that customer selection, so you can ask "what is this specific customer missing" rather than only "what am I missing overall."

Export to Excel Downloads every Sold and Missing SKU across your top groups as one flat, filterable table — Rank, Category, Group, YTD $, Source, Status (Sold/Missing), SKU, and Part Name — scoped to your current Customer selection.
02 — The six pages

The Cancelled Container Orders page

Every container order of yours that was cancelled this year — who, what, how much, and whether credit was a factor.

The cards across the top

Total cancelled dollars, how many orders and order lines that covers, how many customers, and the average size of a cancelled order. The last two cards are about credit: Customers on Credit Hold is the cancelled dollars from customers currently on credit hold (with how many customers that is), and Credit Hold Overridden is the cancelled dollars on orders where a credit hold was overridden (with how many orders).

Cancelled $ by Order Month

Bars are grouped by the month the order was originally placed, not the month it was cancelled.

Breakdown tables

The same cancelled dollars, split By Customer, By Category, By Group, By Warehouse, and By Country & Vendor (one row per vendor, alongside the country it ships from) — each with its share of the total, the number of orders, and the number of lines. Select any column heading to sort by it. The By Customer table also has a Credit Hold column: a red Hold tag marks customers currently on credit hold.

The order list

Below the tables, every cancelled order is listed largest first, with its customer, order date, and number of lines. A red Credit Hold tag means the customer is on credit hold, and a green Crd Hold Overridden tag means a credit hold was overridden on that order. Select any order to see its lines — part, description, category, group, vendor, warehouse, ship ETA, and cancelled dollars.

Filters

Customer is the same shared selection as on the other pages (see Filters that follow you). Category, Warehouse, and Order Month narrow just this page — the cards, chart, every table, and the order list all update together.

Export to Excel Downloads two tabs, both matching your current filters: a Summary tab with each breakdown table (including the Credit Hold column for customers), and an Order Lines tab listing every cancelled line — Order #, Order Date, Customer, Sales Rep, Category, Group, Part, Description, Vendor, Country, Warehouse, Ship ETA, Customer Credit Hold, Credit Override, and Cancelled $.
03 — Good to know

Picking more than one

Every filter in this report — Customer, Category, Subcategory, Vendor, SPIN, Warehouse, Sales Rep, Compare To, Order Month — works the same way: a checklist, not a single pick.

Select the filter to open a checklist. (All) sits at the top, and checking it checks every name below it at once — that's the default, unfiltered state you'll see everywhere. Uncheck any individual name to exclude just that one. Uncheck (All) itself and every name clears together, narrowing the page down to nothing until you check something back on — and checking every individual name back on collapses the list back to (All) automatically. Type in the search box at the top of the list to jump to a name in a long list.

03 — Good to know

Filters that follow you

Pick a customer on any page, and it's already selected when you switch to the others.

Select a customer (or several) on the Dashboard, then switch to Sales Trend — that same selection is already applied there, and the page is already filtered to it. The same goes for Product Images, Collection Sales, and Cancelled Container Orders. You only have to set it once.

If a customer you've selected doesn't exist on one of the other pages, that page falls back to showing everyone (All) rather than showing nothing. If you've deliberately narrowed the filter down to no customers at all, though, that carries over as-is — every page shows nothing until you check a name back on.
One exception L12M Customer Buys doesn't follow this shared selection — it browses every customer company-wide, not just your own, so it keeps its own independent Customer and Compare To pickers instead.
Category, Subcategory, Vendor, SPIN, Warehouse, and Order Month are never shared either — each page keeps its own selection for these, so picking one on Dashboard won't carry over to Sales Trend, Product Images, or Cancelled Container Orders.
03 — Good to know

Exporting to Excel

Every export matches whatever filter you currently have set — and warns you first if that's more than one customer.

Because Customer filters accept multiple selections, it's easy to export a view that quietly combines two or more accounts' numbers into one workbook. Whenever you export with more than one customer selected, a confirmation appears first so that doesn't happen by accident.

Select Cancel to go back and narrow your selection, or Export Anyway if a combined view is exactly what you wanted.

03 — Good to know

Signing out

Select Sign Out in the top-right corner any time.

This clears your session and returns you to the login screen. If you don't sign out, you'll stay logged in on that browser until you close every window — worth signing out manually on a shared or public computer.
